text:
mgu-store

An app store for BMW iDrive 7 and iDrive 8 head units (MGU). Browse,
install, update and remove apps on the car's screen, from GitHub
repositories, web addresses or a USB stick.

It installs:

- the Store app;
- the updater , which downloads and installs what the Store asks for;
- the deploy tool , which performs and can roll back every install;
- app privacy , which keeps installed apps out of the head unit's reports to BMW;
- the renderer , which draws the Store and other apps' graphics;
- Python , for apps the head unit builds from source;
- the internet uplink , for internet through a USB adapter, an LTE stick, a tethered phone or Wi-Fi.

On iDrive 8, installs and removals take effect at the next head-unit
restart.

 Screenshots

The Store: apps and head-unit tools from every source.

 

An app's page, with its source, version and Install.

 

Installed: the apps and tools on the head unit.

 

Settings: sources, Wi-Fi, accounts and phone access.

 

Adding a GitHub repository: pick its releases, tags or a branch.

 

 Requirements

- A computer (Windows 10/11, macOS or Linux, x64 or arm64) with the
 OpenSSH client, which all three have built in.
- Root SSH access to the head unit and root's private key. Tools such as
 idrive7-8-ssh-root
 set it up over an ENET cable.
- A way to reach the head unit's SSH: the car's Wi-Fi hotspot (default
 address 172.16.222.97 ), ENET, or any other SSH route.
- The car parked and on stable power until the install finishes.

 Install

Connect the computer to the head unit (the car's Wi-Fi hotspot or an ENET
cable), then run the installer with root's SSH key:

 

 

It finds the head unit by itself and says which connection it used.
The other commands below ( token , usb-repo , first-install --from ) run
the same way, in place of first-install … in the one-liner.
When the installer asks Restart the head unit now? [y/N] , answer y 
and it restarts the head unit. The Store's tile then appears among the
car's apps, and every later update comes through the Store.

 Option What it does 
 --- --- 
 --identity root's private SSH key 
 --host , --port reach the head unit at this SSH address instead (port 22 unless given); for an SSH config alias, give its port with --port 
 --user SSH user (default root ) 
 --ssh-opt an extra ssh -o option, e.g. ConnectTimeout=30 ; repeatable. Through a jump host, give --host too: --host --ssh-opt ProxyJump= 
 --token asks for a GitHub token, for private repositories 
 --no-uplink leaves out the internet uplink 
 --no-renderer leaves out the renderer 
 --no-restart-prompt ends without asking to restart the head unit 

With Node.js 18 or newer, the installer also runs as
a script:

 

 

 Uninstall

To take the Store off the head unit, run the installer with uninstall 
in place of first-install :

 

 

It lists the apps and tools installed through the Store, including other
repositories' tools, and asks Remove all of it? [y/N] ( --yes answers
for you). It then removes them and everything the setup changed on the
head unit, and the Store's settings and tokens with them. It ends with one
line saying whether anything is left; running it again finishes what is
left. When the head unit needs a restart to finish, it asks
 Restart the head unit now? [y/N] . It finds the head unit the same way
and takes the same SSH options ( --identity , --host , --port , --user ,
 --ssh-opt ).

 Using the Store

The side menu has four pages:

- Store : apps and tools from your sources, with their state (installed,
 update available, restart pending, …).
- Installed : what is installed, with Update and Update all .
- USB : what a plugged-in USB stick offers.
- Settings : sources, Wi-Fi, accounts, proxy, phone access, Check now and
 Restart head unit .

Open an app or tool to install, update or remove it. Updates never install
on their own. Tools marked Restart pending take effect after a head-unit
restart (Settings → Restart head unit ).

 Sources

The Store comes with these sources: this repository,
idrive7-apps,
idrive-apps (with the
renderer that draws on the instrument cluster and the HUD, and the CarPlay
map on the instrument cluster),
car-apps (IterioDev's apps and
tools, most of them for iDrive 8 only, at its newest x.y.z tag) and
idrive7-system-monitor
(System Monitor, iDrive 7 only).

To add one: Settings → Add source , then type owner/repo , a GitHub
link, or the address of a catalog.json ( may be left out). For a GitHub
repository, pick what to follow from what it has: Releases , Tags or
one of its branches.

On iDrive 8, Add source and Add token open the Store's on-screen keyboard
while mgu-render draws the Store. On the Store's widget screens (no
mgu-render), typing doesn't work yet on iDrive 8: add sources and tokens
from the phone page or the computer, or use Sign in with GitHub .

 Private repositories

Add an account in Settings → Accounts :

- Sign in with GitHub : scan the QR code, enter the code on your phone
 and sign in. The repository also needs the
 mgu-store GitHub App installed.
- Add token : a GitHub token. Typing it on the phone page or with
 node mgu-install.js token --identity on the computer is easier
 than on the car.

 Creating a token: 

1. On github.com: your picture → Settings → Developer settings →
 Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens →
 Generate new token .
2. Name it, and pick an expiration ( No expiration keeps the car working).
3. Resource owner : your account, or the organisation that owns the
 repositories. One token covers one owner.
4. Repository access : Only select repositories , and pick the private
 repositories the car should read.
5. Permissions : add Contents , set to Read-only .
6. Generate token and copy it ( github pat … ); GitHub shows it once.

An organisation may have to approve the token first. For a repository of
someone else's account, use a classic token with the repo scope instead.

An app store for BMW iDrive 7 and iDrive 8 head units (MGU). Browse, install, update and remove apps on the car's screen, from GitHub repositories, web addresses or a USB stick.

install.title: Install
install.html:
Connect the computer to the head unit (the car's Wi-Fi hotspot or an ENET cable), then run the installer with root's SSH key:

# macOS, Linux
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/robertnisipeanu/mgu-store/main/deploy/install.sh | sh -s -- first-install --identity ~/.ssh/mgu_root_key

# Windows PowerShell
& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/robertnisipeanu/mgu-store/main/deploy/install.ps1))) first-install --identity $HOME\.ssh\mgu_root_key

It finds the head unit by itself and says which connection it used. The other commands below (token, usb-repo, first-install --from) run the same way, in place of first-install … in the one-liner. When the installer asks Restart the head unit now? [y/N], answer y and it restarts the head unit. The Store's tile then appears among the car's apps, and every later update comes through the Store.

Option What it does
--identity <file> root's private SSH key
--host <address>, --port <n> reach the head unit at this SSH address instead (port 22 unless given); for an SSH config alias, give its port with --port
--user <name> SSH user (default root)
--ssh-opt <option> an extra ssh -o option, e.g. ConnectTimeout=30; repeatable. Through a jump host, give --host too: --host <head unit> --ssh-opt ProxyJump=<jump host>
--token asks for a GitHub token, for private repositories
--no-uplink leaves out the internet uplink
--no-renderer leaves out the renderer
--no-restart-prompt ends without asking to restart the head unit

With Node.js 18 or newer, the installer also runs as a script:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/robertnisipeanu/mgu-store/main/deploy/mgu-install.js | node - first-install --identity ~/.ssh/mgu_root_key

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/robertnisipeanu/mgu-store/main/deploy/mgu-install.js -OutFile mgu-install.js; if ($?) { node mgu-install.js first-install --identity $HOME\.ssh\mgu_root_key }

usage.title: Using the Store
usage.html:
The side menu has four pages:

  • Store: apps and tools from your sources, with their state (installed, update available, restart pending, …).
  • Installed: what is installed, with Update and Update all.
  • USB: what a plugged-in USB stick offers.
  • Settings: sources, Wi-Fi, accounts, proxy, phone access, Check now and Restart head unit.

Open an app or tool to install, update or remove it. Updates never install on their own. Tools marked Restart pending take effect after a head-unit restart (Settings → Restart head unit).

Sources

The Store comes with these sources: this repository, idrive7-apps, idrive-apps (with the renderer that draws on the instrument cluster and the HUD, and the CarPlay map on the instrument cluster), car-apps (IterioDev's apps and tools, most of them for iDrive 8 only, at its newest x.y.z tag) and idrive7-system-monitor (System Monitor, iDrive 7 only).

To add one: Settings → Add source, then type owner/repo, a GitHub link, or the address of a catalog.json (https:// may be left out). For a GitHub repository, pick what to follow from what it has: Releases, Tags or one of its branches.

On iDrive 8, Add source and Add token open the Store's on-screen keyboard while mgu-render draws the Store. On the Store's widget screens (no mgu-render), typing doesn't work yet on iDrive 8: add sources and tokens from the phone page or the computer, or use Sign in with GitHub.

Private repositories

Add an account in Settings → Accounts:

  • Sign in with GitHub: scan the QR code, enter the code on your phone and sign in. The repository also needs the mgu-store GitHub App installed.
  • Add token: a GitHub token. Typing it on the phone page or with node mgu-install.js token --identity <key> on the computer is easier than on the car.

Creating a token:

  1. On github.com: your picture → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens → Generate new token.
  2. Name it, and pick an expiration (No expiration keeps the car working).
  3. Resource owner: your account, or the organisation that owns the repositories. One token covers one owner.
  4. Repository access: Only select repositories, and pick the private repositories the car should read.
  5. Permissions: add Contents, set to Read-only.
  6. Generate token and copy it (github_pat_…); GitHub shows it once.

An organisation may have to approve the token first. For a repository of someone else's account, use a classic token with the repo scope instead.

Phone page

Settings → Phone access → On shows a QR code. Scan it with a phone on the car's hotspot to see sources, installs, errors and logs, and to add sources and accounts with the phone's keyboard. Turn it off when done.

Internet

The internet uplink gives the updater and apps that need it internet through:

  • a USB Ethernet adapter;
  • an LTE stick (e.g. Huawei E3372h);
  • an Android phone with USB tethering;
  • an iPhone with Personal Hotspot on, kept unlocked (tap Trust when asked); its USB music playback stops while it tethers;
  • Wi-Fi, such as a phone's hotspot: Settings → Wi-Fi. The car's own hotspot and wireless CarPlay keep working beside it. On iDrive 7 units with a Broadcom radio, WPA3-only networks can't be joined.

The Store shows Online once connected.

Proxy

Where GitHub is slow or blocked, the updater can download through a proxy on the same network, such as Clash on a computer or a router: Settings → Proxy, turn it on and type its address, http://192.168.8.1:7890 or socks5://192.168.8.1:7891. A proxy that wants a password takes it as socks5://user:password@192.168.8.1:7891. Everything the updater downloads goes through it, and builds on the unit too. Turn it off to download directly again. The phone page has the same setting.

Usage statistics

Once a day, the Store's updater sends a small anonymous report, to show how many cars use the Store, which apps and sources are used and which installs fail. It is on by default; turn it off in Settings → Share usage statistics. Off, nothing is sent and what was waiting to be sent is deleted.

What a report contains

  • iDrive 7 or 8, the hardware variant and the firmware version (its build train, such as P18_23w44.2)
  • the versions of the Store, the updater, the deploy tool, the renderer and the uplink, when they came from a public source or the installer
  • the apps and tools installed from public GitHub sources (id and version), and the names of those sources
  • since the last report: first installs from public sources, failed installs (the app's id and a fixed reason code such as download or build, never the error text), and public sources added or removed
  • whether it is the car's first report ever and its first this month, and whether the Store was installed within the last day

What it never contains

  • anything about private sources (ones that need a sign-in) or anything installed from them; https catalogs, folders and USB sticks other than a copy of a public source are left out too
  • an id of the car, the head unit or the install, the VIN, location, account names, tokens, Wi-Fi details or logs

What is kept

  • The server keeps only daily and monthly totals (for example "cars on iDrive 8 today" or "cars with this app version"); single reports are never stored.
  • The IP address is neither stored nor logged. The country is taken from it for the totals; a salted hash of it is used only for the server's short-term rate limit.
  • Data is held on Cloudflare in the EU.

The report is one HTTPS request with a 10-second limit. If it can't be sent, nothing else is affected; it is tried again at the next check that day. The updater's README shows a sample report.

Questions: open an issue in this repository.
